title: #005. Precision Alloy Blending
subtitle: Turn percentage composition bounds into clean linear equalities and inequalities for a fixed batch size.
markdown:
# #005. Precision Alloy Blending

<!-- section:scenario -->
A metallurgy plant must blend raw ingot lots $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ into an exact batch weight of **`targetBatch` kg** of high-grade alloy. Each raw metal $i$ costs `costs[i]` per kg, has available stock `availabilities[i]` kg, and contains fraction `compositions[i][k]` of chemical element $k$.

Quality control mandates that in the final batch, the mass fraction of each element $k$ lies between `minRatios[k]` and `maxRatios[k]`. Find the non-negative blending weights `amounts[i]` minimizing total material cost.

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P005Input`)**:
  - `targetBatch: number` — required exact total weight of the alloy batch
  - `costs: number[]` — cost per kg of raw metal $i$
  - `availabilities: number[]` — maximum stock (kg) of raw metal $i$
  - `compositions: number[][]` — `compositions[i][k]` is the mass fraction of element $k$ in metal $i$
  - `minRatios: number[]` — minimum allowed mass fraction of element $k$
  - `maxRatios: number[]` — maximum allowed mass fraction of element $k$
- **Output (`P005Output`)**:
  - `amounts: number[]` — kg used of each raw metal
  - `totalCost: number` — minimized material cost

<!-- section:example -->
With `targetBatch = 100`, costs `[300, 500, 400]`, and elements requiring $\ge 35\%$ of Element 0, $\ge 30\%$ of Element 1, and $\le 25\%$ of Element 2:

- Metal 0 alone (`300`/kg) lacks Element 0 (`20% < 35%`).
- Blending **`amounts = [62.5, 37.5, 0]`** yields Element 0 $= 0.2(62.5) + 0.6(37.5) = 35$ kg (`35%`), Element 1 $= 0.5(62.5) + 0.2(37.5) = 38.75$ kg (`38.75%`), and Element 2 $= 0.1(62.5) + 0.4(37.5) = 21.25$ kg (`21.25%`) at minimum cost **`37,500`**.

<!-- section:hint1 -->
Writing `elemWeight / sum(amounts) >= minRatio` looks nonlinear at first glance. Why is it actually a pure linear constraint in this problem? Because total weight `sum(amounts)` is constrained to equal the constant `targetBatch`! Multiply both sides by `targetBatch`.

<!-- section:hint2 -->
The `amounts` variables (already bounded by `[0, availabilities[i]]`) are declared in the starter code. Enforce `sum(amounts) == targetBatch` and for each element $k$ enforce:
- `sum_i compositions[i][k] * amounts[i] >= minRatios[k] * targetBatch`
- `sum_i compositions[i][k] * amounts[i] <= maxRatios[k] * targetBatch`

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} c_i x_i \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i = B \\
& L_k B \le \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} p_{i,k} x_i \le U_k B && \forall k \\
& 0 \le x_i \le A_i && \forall i
\end{aligned}
$$

Whenever the denominator of a percentage specification is a fixed batch size $B$, clearing the denominator keeps the entire problem in clean LP form. (Chapter 2 covers the variable-denominator fractional case!)

judge.m0: Output must be an object { amounts, totalCost }.
judge.m6: Reported totalCost ({p0}) does not match computed cost ({p1}).
judge.m7: Valid blend, but cost ({p0}) exceeds the LP minimum ({p1}).
